newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down on poor sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down on Thursday due to poor sentiment on rumours that concrete measures will be announced to force domestic investors out of the market, brokers said.
The index edged down 0.082 points or 0.13 percent to 60.779 points, on volume of 18.3 million shares worth $6.9 million against $9.1 million on Wednesday.

Brokers said market sentiment remained weak due to the rumours that the stock exchange was planning specific measures to restrict domestic investors from buying B shares in response to Beijing's reaffirmation of the policy on Wednesday.

"The rumours led investors to recall the fact that the index hit a record low around 45 points (in November 1996) after the exchange announced the ban in line with Beijing's demands, even though it was not seriously implemented," one broker said.
"Most institutions were seen cutting their positions to avoid risk given the uncertainties although there was some speculative support buying," he added.
"The index will slip further to test the 58-point support level on Friday," a second broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded with 20 down, four flat and 18 up.
Real estate developer Shanghai Jinqiao was the biggest loser on concerns about its results, falling $0.020 or 4.16 percent to $0.460 on volume of 485,000 shares.
Hua Xin Cement followed on expectations of unpromising results, slipping $0.010 or 4.13 percent to $0.232 on volume of 484,000 shares.
Newcomer clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was the most active share and became the star on institutional support, rising $0.012 or 3.94 percent to $0.316 on volume of 6.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share market ended up on a technical rebound, but trading remained sluggish with market sentiment cautious, brokers said.

The A index rose 11.391 points or 1.22 percent to 947.042 points, on volume of 225.7 million shares worth 2.1 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index was up 23.662 points or 0.99 percent at 2418.650 points.
Clothing maker Kansai was the star on institutional demand, jumping 10 percent to its limit-up of 17.17 yuan on volume of 924,200 million shares.
